rationale: The screenplay is a highly faithful, nearly scene-by-scene adaptation of Margery Williams Bianco's original text (as provided in book_indexed.txt), preserving the complete narrative arc from Christmas stocking introduction, Skin Horse philosophy, progressive shabbiness through love, garden/wood sequences, scarlet fever crisis, bonfire abandonment, tear-induced Fairy intervention, magical transformation, and poignant final reunion. All major beats, symbolic elements (sawdust heart, hind legs, tear-to-flower, Real vs. unreal), and seasonal progression are covered without invented plot, omissions of consequence, or alterations to themes of love, beauty, and becoming Real. Character descriptions are stable and visually rich (e.g., Rabbit's initial 'fat and bunchy' velveteen with pink sateen ears evolving explicitly to threadbare, whiskerless, spotted remnants then to 'brown fur, soft and shiny' with twitching ears; Skin Horse's bald seams and pulled tail; Nana's aproned practicality; Doctor's brisk suit; Fairy's pearl/dew-drop gown; Boy's age-appropriate flannel-to-outdoor-clothes progression across eras), enabling clear casting and consistent photoreal tracking across toy-to-living states per the VISION_META. AI video directibility is strong with concrete, observable actions (wheelbarrow rides, ant-watching, specific hops/dances, tear drop, blossom opening, hind-leg scratch-to-leap, shadow dancing on grass) sized for clips, but occasional narrator VO summaries and internal 'knowing'/'longing' statements slightly dilute pure 'show, don't tell' camera readability. Dramatic pacing mirrors the book's gentle, episodic build-up and emotional crescendos (happy love → anxious illness → despair → magical joy → quiet resolution) with effective time transitions ('weeks pass', seasonal shifts) and a clean three-act-like structure ending in FADE OUT. Dialogue is almost verbatim from the source (Skin Horse's full 'Real' explanation, wild rabbits' taunting, Boy's 'He's REAL!', Fairy's nursery magic speech, final Boy recognition), retaining philosophical subtext on love's transformative power without modernization. Sound design and scoring are evocative and period-appropriate (rustling tissue, clock ticks, birdsong, wheel squeaks, fever murmurs, single tear drop, luminous fairy chimes, joyful thumps, resolving warm theme), enhancing magic and emotion without overpowering the intimate live-action style. Minor deductions reflect residual telling in a few summary beats and the inherent challenge of photoreal animals 'speaking' (though book dialogues are preserved faithfully). No deal-breakers; fully productionReady for the locked photoreal early-20th-century style.
